summary:
Package B is done and the hull builds as one solid with all three changes, verified in a full build_hull_only build plus before/after renders.

1. Strake: a slim rounded rail, 58 mm high and 26 mm proud (1.9 x 0.9 mm in the model), replaces the 95 x 55 square bar. Its top and crown are rounded and its underside ends at 45 deg against the hull, so it prints without overhang. It is one smooth loft (no ruled facets) along a smooth path, wraps the stern corner without the old 16/10/26 deg knuckles, crosses the transom, and dives smoothly into the hull at the bow instead of ending in a flat face.

2. Transom corners: the side/transom corners are now rounded, built into transom_cutter (OCC fillets fail there). In each horizontal level the cutter follows the transom, then curves forward in an arc that meets the hull side with a small leftover kink of 7 deg, so the boolean never has touching tangent surfaces. The geometry comes from C.section, so it follows package A's new sections. The rounding fades out below the waterline, so the bottom edge stays crisp as on IMG_9391. The transom on the centreline, its rake and the rudder-pin zone are unchanged.
   - Not done: the transom top edge (transom to deck) is still sharp. A cutter built from horizontal levels cannot round a horizontal edge, and I did not try another method.

3. Keel root: KEEL_FILLET is now used. The keel sections flare out towards the hull and meet the canoe bottom at about 30 deg, which gives a visible fillet instead of a sharp crease, with no OCC fillet.

Decision for you: I changed build.py, which is outside my package. OCC's default Volume() is wrong by up to about 90 L on the trimmed smooth faces these lofts create. robust_union compares volumes, so it rejected the deck-fittings union and the build failed, even with the corner rounding switched off. robust_union now falls back to an exact volume calculation, but only when the fast check says no. This made the fittings step about 150 s slower. The hull build took 350 s against 153 s for the baseline, but other builds were running at the same time, so that timing is rough. Without this change my package does not build; it only touches robust_union, far from export().

changes.what: transom_cutter: for the hull cut (offset 0) it builds a cutter with rounded corners, a degree-3 loft through horizontal levels every 50 mm from z -450 to 1150. If that fails it prints a warning and falls back to the old prism (now _plain_cutter). offset != 0 (the name relief) still gets the old prism. New helpers at the end of the file compute the corner from the curve API: _side_y, _side_psi, _transom_psi, _corner, _corner_arc, _stern_plans, _stern_plan, _cutter_wire, _rounded_cutter. Arc radius is TRANSOM_CORNER_L/tan(corner angle/2), at most 5 x that, and the arc turns the corner angle minus the 7 deg exit. Below the waterline the arc is moved out of the hull (no rounding there), it is frozen just under the deck edge, and the arc values are lightly smoothed in z. _side_frame now copes with sections that are not monotonic in z. _strake_path is rewritten: dense points along the side at strake_z, light smoothing, then the same corner arc as the cutter, a short smooth join where the arc meets the side, and across the transom to the centreline, with a hull normal at each point. New _strake_profile (rounded profile with a buried back, one closed curve). rubbing_strake: one smooth loft through the same profile every ~100 mm from port bow round the transom to starboard bow, with a 250 mm dive at each bow end. New _loft3 helper (degree-3 ThruSections): the default loft (up to degree 8) gave a self-intersecting strake and a wrong cutter. hull_solid and _section_wire are not touched.

keel(): uses KEEL_FILLET. It finds the height where the keel meets the canoe bottom (mean along the root, about z=-489, within about 7 mm). It adds 8 flared foil sections between 0.7*KEEL_FILLET above and KEEL_FILLET below that height: 0.75*KEEL_FILLET wider at the junction, meeting the bottom at 30 deg, and tangent to the keel side lower down. The top section 260 mm into the hull and the original sections below the fillet are kept. Lofted with degree 3 (_loft3). New helpers _offset_foil_wire, _keel_fillet_offset, _le_z, _loft3; imports numpy. rudder() is unchanged.

Next to TRANSOM_*: TRANSOM_CORNER_L = 110 (width of the rounded band on the transom; 0 gives the old sharp corner), TRANSOM_CORNER_EXIT = 7 deg, TRANSOM_CORNER_Z = (-220, -100) for the fade below the waterline, with a comment. Strake block: STRAKE_H 95 -> 58, STRAKE_PROUD 55 -> 26, new STRAKE_BURY = 30, STRAKE_TAPER = 250, STRAKE_STEP = 100; STRAKE_X0 unchanged at 200; comment updated with the photo and Bambu references. KEEL_FILLET value unchanged; comment now says how it is used.

Outside my package, but needed for the build. New _volume() with an exact OCC volume calculation; robust_union accepts a candidate if either the fast Volume() check or the exact one shows growth. The exact one only runs when the fast one says no.

measurements:
Final build (worktree as patched, build_hull_only, 40 stations, STL 0.018 mm abs / 0.12 rad): exit 0, one hull solid. Mesh has 4 shells: the outer hull plus 3 cavity shells. Plastic 228 cm3 (baseline 228). STL 17.7 MB. Model bbox 264.9 x 89.4 x 104.8 mm (baseline 266.0 x 89.4 x 104.8).

Main dimensions: LOA 7949.7 (baseline 7984.7, because the old 55 mm bar stuck out aft of the transom). Beam 2680.6 (unchanged). Draft 1400.0 (unchanged).

Fine STL (0.01 mm abs, scratch copy with the same geometry), compared with baseline_fine.stl:
- Transom on the centreline: z=-200 and -90 (rudder pins) +0.0 mm; z=0 -1.0; z=400 -0.3; z=700 -0.1; z=900 0.0.
- Deck edge at x=7300-7850: largest change 0.3 mm (x=7850).
- Material removed by the corner rounding: 1.1 L (signed STL volume, both sides).

Strake: rail size is 58 x 26 mm (30 mm buried) by construction; my STL readout of the rail size was unreliable because of the deck structures, so these are not measured values. Strake union step 9-23 s (baseline 52 s); strake loft valid, no self-intersection. Path around the corner is smooth, tightest bend about 170 mm radius where the hull side itself curves.

Corner angle before rounding: 19-38 deg from z=-60 to 740, falling to 8 deg at the deck edge. After: rounded band about 70-190 mm wide on the transom, 7 deg leftover kink where it meets the side.

meshcheck: final STL 10 non-manifold edges; fine STL 120; baseline fine STL 124. I did not check whether they come from the mesher or the geometry.

Volume check: on the hull after the rounded cut, default Volume() was +65 L wrong against the exact value (the exact value matches the STL to 0.5 L). After keel + strake + fittings it was +90 L wrong; for the old prism cut the error is 0.7 L.
open_issues: build.py (outside my package): robust_union now falls back to an exact volume when the fast Volume() check fails. Needed because OCC's default Volume() is tens of litres wrong on trimmed smooth loft faces; without it the fittings union is rejected even with the corner rounding off. Merge it, or move the same fix wherever package D wants it. Cost: about 150 s in the fittings step on a loaded machine.
Transom top edge (transom to deck) is still sharp. A cutter built from horizontal levels cannot round it; I did not try another method (for example a second rounding cutter along the top edge).
The corner rounding leaves a deliberate 7 deg kink where it meets the hull side (TRANSOM_CORNER_EXIT) so the boolean stays robust. Smaller values were not tested.

The corner rounding is computed from C.section, so it follows package A's new sections automatically. But after merging with A, rebuild and check: TRANSOM_CORNER_Z assumes the transom bottom is near z=-255, and the cutter raises an error if the corner lies outboard of the y=450 parking position below the waterline. The width of the rounding will change with A's new section shape.

A combined build with packages A and C has not been run, only my worktree. TRANSOM_CORNER_L = 0 gives the old sharp transom if the rounding causes trouble after merging; strake and keel fillet work either way.
Pulpit-leg hole at x=900 (fittings.py, package C) breaks out through the topside right at the strake. It was there before, but shows more on the slim rail (cmp_liste_baug.png).

The anchor-roller block (|y|<85, x 170-690, package C) overlaps the strake's diving bow end (inner edge reaches y about 50 at x=200). The unions pass now. If C keeps the big block and trouble appears, raise STRAKE_X0 to about 300.
The visible strake starts at about x=255: the rail emerges about 55 mm after STRAKE_X0=200, where its 250 mm dive into the hull begins.
meshcheck reports 10 non-manifold edges on the final STL (fine-tolerance STL 120, baseline 124); I did not trace them. The solid itself is checked to be one piece by build_hull.
I could not measure the strake's proud/height reliably from the STL (my readout was confused by the deck structures). The 58 x 26 mm are construction values, confirmed only visually in the renders.
